title: On-call rota — Q1
text: Northwind production on-call, times in UTC. Weekdays 00:00-08:00 primary is SRE-A (Jordan Hale), secondary SRE-B (Samir Patel). Weekdays 08:00-16:00 primary SRE-B, secondary SRE-C (Riley Chen). Weekdays 16:00-24:00 primary SRE-C, secondary SRE-A. Saturday and Sunday all hours: primary SRE-B, secondary SRE-C. Escalation owner is the secondary. The incident commander for Sev-1 is the primary. Pager rotation ignores regional holidays.

title: Sev-2 runbook: datastore hot shard
text: Sev-2 datastore hot shard. Step 1: confirm the firing shard from the alert label `shard_id` and the shard topology note. Step 2: isolate the failing shard by removing it from the serving pool (`shardctl drain <id>`). Do not drain a shard during an active change freeze unless the freeze calendar exception 'sev2-mitigation' applies. Step 3: page the escalation owner listed on the rota (the secondary). Step 4: if drain does not drop error rate 50% in 10 minutes, fail over the region using the topology note's failover target. Step 5: file IR-SEV2 with the shard id and the freeze exception used, if any.

title: Shard topology
text: shard-a lives in us-east and fails over to shard-c. shard-b lives in eu-west and fails over to shard-d. shard-c is the us-east standby and is not customer-serving unless shard-a is drained. shard-d is the eu-west standby. Customer checkout traffic hashes to shard-b when the customer region is EU. US checkout hashes to shard-a. Never drain shard-c and shard-a at the same time.

title: Change freeze calendar
text: A production change freeze runs every year from 15 December 00:00 UTC through 2 January 23:59 UTC. During freeze, deploys to eu-west and us-east are blocked. Exception codes: 'sev1-restore' (Sev-1 only) and 'sev2-mitigation' (drain or failover listed in the Sev-2 runbook). Feature flags and documentation edits are allowed. Schema migrations are not allowed under any exception.

title: Lab sample chain-of-custody SOP
text: Samples arriving at Dock B get form COC-1 at the dock, then form COC-2 when placed in freezer F-2. COC-1 must be completed before the sample leaves the dock. If freezer F-2 is in alarm, do not open F-2; transfer is delayed and form COC-3 (delay log) is filed after COC-1 and before any later COC-2. Courier IDs are copied onto COC-1. Aliquots are never created at the dock.

title: Freezer F-2 alarm procedure
text: Freezer F-2 alarm. First action: silence the audible alarm on panel P-4; do not open F-2. Second: read the display temperature. If warmer than -60 C, page Facilities-Night and the lab duty scientist. Third: start a temperature log every 5 minutes. Samples already inside F-2 stay inside until Facilities clears the alarm. Incoming samples follow the chain-of-custody SOP delay path (COC-3). Do not move F-2 samples to F-1 without a dual sign-off on form MOVE-7.

title: Lab duty roster
text: Lab duty scientist weekday days (08:00-20:00 local) is Dr. Ines Vogel. Night and weekend duty is Dr. Marcus Adeyemi. Facilities-Night is on radio channel 4 after 18:00 local. Dock B is staffed until 17:00 local; after 17:00 inbound samples wait in the lockbox and still require COC-1 before freezer transfer the next morning.

title: Status page rules
text: Customer-facing status is updated only by the incident commander (Sev-1 primary, Sev-2 primary). Do not name internal shard ids on the public page. EU checkout degradation is described as 'EU checkout delays' when shard-b is drained. Internal tickets still use shard ids.
